one_line_contribution: That the raw-vs-distilled experience-memory disagreement is not about abstraction level at all but about two nameable content cues — source-scene object-to-receptacle bindings and failed-action-to-repair pairs — which can be annotated deterministically from ALFWorld logs and transplanted into and out of any representation at matched injected tokens, with the binding cue predicted to help only when the evaluation scene overlaps the memory pool's scenes and to actively harm otherwise.
closest_prior_work: The strongest threat I verified is arXiv:2604.14004, 'Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents' (2026-04-15, s2 verified), which already reports the proposal's headline interaction as an empirical design principle: 'abstraction dictates transferability; high-level insights generalize well, whereas low-level traces often induce negative transfer due to excessive specificity.' That is P1 (raw wins where the source context recurs, abstraction wins where it does not) plus the sign of P3 (over-specific detail causes negative transfer), already published, in coding agents across domains rather than in ALFWorld across room instances. It does not match tokens, does not name the cue classes inside the items, and does not transplant cues, so it does not scoop the identification design — but it removes most of the surprise from the proposal's two most prominent predictions, and the proposal neither cites nor found it. Second, arXiv:2506.06698 (CER, ACL, verified, 47 citations) already partitions accumulated experience into 'environment dynamics' and 'skills' — very nearly the binding-vs-procedure split the proposal presents as new — and arXiv:2604.05533 (Echo, verified) decomposes prior interactions into five knowledge dimensions for transfer to unseen tasks. The genuinely unclaimed part is narrow: the deterministic cue annotation, the plus/minus transplant at a matched token band, and the seen/unseen scene split as the moderator. SkillEvolBench (arXiv:2605.24117, verified on both s2 and hf) remains the proposal's correct anchor and does leave the cues unnamed, as claimed.
strongest_objection: The headline claim — P5, 'after conditioning on the two cue indicators the residual representation effect is within MDE of zero' — is neither causally identified nor adequately powered, and it is the only prediction that would actually establish 'abstraction is not the variable.' (a) Identification: for the six base representations the cue indicators are caused by the representation, so conditioning on them to read off a 'residual representation main effect' is a controlled-direct-effect estimand that requires no unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding. Representations differ in register, imperative-vs-narrative form, step granularity, item count at fixed budget, and ordering — all plausible mediator-outcome confounders. The transplants do randomize cues within a representation, which is the right instrument, but the transplant arms only cover R1/R3/R5, while P5's falsification condition is stated over skill and graph (R4/R6), where no randomization exists at all. (b) Collinearity: by the stated annotation rule, essentially every raw trajectory contains a scene binding and essentially no insight does, so within the base cells the cue indicator is close to a deterministic function of representation and the model cannot separate them; the manual audit addresses annotator recall but not this near-collinearity. (c) Power: MDE is pre-registered at about 5 points net at n=400, but every prediction that matters is evaluated within a split at n=200, where MDE is roughly 7 points, and P2/P3/P4 are stated as fractions ('at least 70 percent', 'more than half') of raw's seen-scene advantage — an advantage this program's own starting position puts at +0.6 points on the 27B and +7.7 for SEC on the 120B. If raw's seen advantage is 6 points, 70 percent of it is 4 points, well inside noise at n=200 with 3 seeds. The confirmatory design is therefore built to test ratios of a quantity that may itself sit at the detection threshold, and a null P5 will be indistinguishable from an underpowered P5.
what_would_fix_it: Three fixes, in order of importance. (1) Stop estimating 'abstraction per se' as a residual after conditioning on a post-treatment mediator. Extend the transplant grid to all six representations so every cue level is randomized within every representation; then the abstraction effect is the representation main effect in a fully crossed randomized design and needs no mediation assumption. Report it as a pre-registered equivalence test against a stated margin, not as a failure to reject. (2) Fix the power arithmetic before the confirmatory run: pilot raw's seen-scene advantage first, and if it is under about 10 points, either raise n per split (the local pool has 1,465 tasks, so 400 per split is achievable) or restate P2/P3/P4 as absolute point differences with pre-registered margins instead of percentages of a small effect. (3) Add the oracle-binding positive control described under missing_baseline, which is what makes P3 a mechanism result rather than a token-cost result. Two smaller repairs: pre-register the truncation rule for P6 (truncating raw from the front versus the back decides P6's outcome, since repair pairs sit late), and pre-register the room-level split before looking at outcomes, since the stated fallback to room-type splitting would gut the binding contrast and must not be chosen after seeing results.
missing_baseline: A correct-bindings-for-the-evaluation-scene arm on the unseen split: an oracle 60-token binding table describing the true object-receptacle layout of the room the agent is actually in, injected in the same slot and token band as the foreign table. Without it, P3's 'foreign bindings are harmful' is confounded with 'any binding table is useless or distracting once the scene is unfamiliar.' The relevance-matched decoy controls token load but not binding format — it does not show that a correctly-bound table in the same format would have helped. With the oracle arm, foreign-below-decoy-below-oracle is decisive evidence that the harm is wrong content adopted as fact, which is exactly what the first-move mediation analysis is supposed to demonstrate. A second omission a reviewer will raise: no retrieval-matched control isolating how much of the seen-scene advantage is retrieval selecting a near-duplicate task instance rather than the binding cue itself; retrieval overlap between the seen split and the pool should be measured and reported as a covariate.

I could not verify anything for the proposal's claim that no LLM-agent work studies the seen-versus-unseen binding mechanism beyond the empty search result, and an empty search is empty, not evidence. Judging the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above average for this pipeline — four named queries, IDs attached, honest disclosure that the WebSearch arm was not run and that direct S2 calls returned HTTP 429. But it is not clean. It missed arXiv:2604.14004, which states the proposal's P1/P3 direction as a finding; it missed arXiv:2607.13884, which already mines correction patterns as the reusable unit; and its fourth query ('scene-specific object location memory ALFWorld seen unseen ...') returned only vision papers and was read as confirming novelty, which is precisely the inference the review rules forbid — the query was too ALFWorld-specific to find the coding-agent and web-agent statements of the same mechanism, and a broader phrasing finds them in one call.
